title: Bias-Corrected Multiplier Bootstrap Inference for Spectral Edges of Large Covariance Matrices
summary: Inference for spectral edges of large covariance matrices is a fundamental problem in high-dimensional statistics. A major difficulty is that the largest non-spiked sample eigenvalues, which serve as natural estimators of the edge, fluctuate on the Tracy--Widom scale. Consequently, valid inference requires accurate centering by the deterministic spectral edge together with a precise scaling constant, both of which are often difficult to estimate in practice under general unknown population covariance structures.
